title: Explicit pin resolver: unified semantics for commit-hash, semver ranges, and moving tags
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Users need deterministic, auditable rules for pinning models in the Redwood API/SDK. Current behavior has implicit precedence and subtle runtime fallbacks that have caused surprise rollouts and variant flips. This ticket specifies a single pin resolver with clear precedence, stability windows for moving tags, compatibility rules between selector types (commit hash, semver, tag), and performance-profile binding semantics that allow runtime routing and fallback without surprising client-side semantics.

Goals:
- Define canonical selector syntax and precedence for API and SDKs.
- Guarantee resolution determinism (same selector resolves to same model reference across control planes within a short time window).
- Define stability window semantics for moving tags ("prod", "stable", "latest") to avoid mid-request shifts and provide predictable rollouts.
- Publish a model performance_profile binding rule so SDKs and runtime can choose compatible quantized/fast variants without changing the pin semantics.
- Provide migration strategy for existing pinned references and a compat mode for older clients.

Proposed selector grammar (examples, human readable):
- Explicit commit: model-name@commit:7b4f2a (absolute, immutable).
- Exact semver: model-name@semver:1.4.2 (bind to exact release artifact).
- Semver range: model-name@semver:^1.4.0 (choose highest matching release satisfying range at resolution time).
- Tag (moving alias): model-name@tag:prod (resolves to an artifact at resolution time with a stability window).
- Floating latest: model-name@latest (alias to tag:latest; discouraged for production).

Precedence rules (deterministic, highest-first):
1) commit (immutable)
2) exact semver
3) semver range (choose highest matching semver at resolution time)
4) tag alias (moving; resolved artifcat pinned to a stability window)
5) unpinned (server default)

Stability windows for tags:
- When a tag moves, the control plane records a move with a timestamp and new target commit. All resolutions within a configurable stability window (default 10 minutes) that were previously resolved to the old target should remain bound to the old commit for in-flight safety. New resolutions after the window may return the new target.
- Tags may be marked "immediate" when controlled rollouts are intentional (admin flag), which short-circuits the window but requires explicit approval.

Performance profile binding:
- Models publish canonical performance_profile ids (e.g., pp-mlperf-1.0) in the model catalog. The resolver returns two things to the client: resolved_artifact_ref (immutable commit ref) and performance_profile id.
- SDKs can request a preferred runtime_variant (e.g., fp16, int8, quantized) but the resolved_artifact_ref remains authoritative. The runtime may route to a compatible fast variant when configured and will report the actual serving_variant in response metadata.

Fallbacks and runtime behavior:
- If a pinned commit is missing on a particular runtime pool, the smart routing layer can fall back according to policy: (a) identical artifact in another region, (b) compatible semver variant, (c) pre-approved fallback model (configured in tenant settings). Fallback is recorded as a policy event and surfaced in Console alerts.

Compatibility and migration:
- Introduce resolver v2 in the control plane. Older clients continue to use resolver v1 semantics by default for 90 days. Admins can opt-in tenants to v2 early.
- Add a migration job that scans existing pinned references and annotates moving tags with stability metadata.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Control plane exposes a Pin Resolve API that returns resolved_artifact_ref, bound_performance_profile_id, resolved_at timestamp, and serving_variant hints.
- SDKs (JS + Python) implement selector syntax parsing and call the new resolver endpoint when pin provided.
- Analytics show deterministic resolution: identical selector + timestamp window => same resolved_artifact_ref in 99.99% of calls across regions.
- A canary rollout demonstrates tag move with stability window preventing mid-request switches.

Out of scope: runtime kernel selection heuristics for quantized artifacts; model training or artifact creation tooling (only referencing published artifacts).

acceptance_criteria: Control plane returns resolved_artifact_ref and performance_profile in Pin Resolve API for all selector types.
SDKs parse selector grammar and use resolver v2 when tenant opt-in is set; fallback to v1 for legacy clients.
Stability window for tag moves enforced in staging canary: no mid-request flips observed during test run.
Telemetry: percent of resolutions that changed artifact between subsequent calls for same selector within default stability window must be < 0.01%.
Console shows tag move history, resolved artifact, and serving_variant on per-request traces.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy resolver v2 behind feature flag for internal tenants. Run e2e suite and synthetic load tests.
Phase 2 (canary): opt-in small set of customers with low-traffic tier. Monitor resolution determinism and fallback events for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual): expose tenant opt-in toggle in Console and CLI. Provide migration tool to annotate existing tags with stability metadata.
Phase 4 (default): after 90 days and no major incidents, flip default resolver to v2 and deprecate v1 with 30-day notice.
decision_record: Use commit > exact semver > semver-range > tag precedence to maximize determinism and support immutable artifacts.
Introduce a default 10-minute stability window for tag moves; provide an 'immediate' administrative override subject to audit logs.
Publish performance_profile bindings at resolution time; runtime may advertise serving_variant but must not change resolved_artifact_ref returned to client.
Provide backward compatibility path: resolver v1 maintained for 90 days with tenant opt-in to v2.
